subtitle: Develop musical phrasing using bends, vibrato, and timing to create expressive lead guitar lines.

introduction.title: Expression: The Soul of Lead Guitar
introduction.text: Two guitarists can play the same notes but create completely different emotional experiences through phrasing and expression. Think of your guitar solo as speaking -- use musical punctuation, questions, answers, and emphasis to tell a story.

columns.title: It's Not What You Play, It's How You Play It
columns.text: A simple G-B-D arpeggio can sound happy (bright attack, quick notes) or sad (bent notes, slow vibrato, soft attack).

columns.title: Musical Conversation
columns.text: Phrasing Elements: Attacks, rests, bends, vibrato, dynamics, note duration, rhythmic placement.

cards.title: String Bending
cards.description: Change pitch by physically bending the string

fields.label: Application
fields.value: Express emotion, reach chord tones, create blues feeling

fields.label: Examples
fields.value: B.B. King vibrato bends, David Gilmour sustained bends

cards.title: Vibrato
cards.description: Slight, rapid pitch variations to add warmth and sustain

fields.label: Application
fields.value: Add life to sustained notes, personal expression signature

fields.label: Examples
fields.value: Gary Moore wide vibrato, Yngwie narrow vibrato

cards.title: Legato Playing
cards.description: Smooth, connected notes using hammer-ons and pull-offs

fields.label: Application
fields.value: Create flowing melodic lines, reduce pick attack

fields.label: Examples
fields.value: Allan Holdsworth fluid lines, Joe Satriani legato runs

cards.title: Rhythmic Displacement
cards.description: Playing notes slightly ahead or behind the beat

fields.label: Application
fields.value: Create groove, add tension, match song feel

fields.label: Examples
fields.value: John Mayer laid-back blues, Steve Vai rhythmic complexity

cards.title: Vocal Melodies
cards.description: Play phrases that could be sung, with natural breaks for "breathing"

fields.label: Concept
fields.value: Breathing and Natural Phrasing

fields.label: Exercise
fields.value: Sing a melody first, then play it on guitar maintaining the vocal phrasing

cards.title: Speech Patterns
cards.description: Create musical conversations with call-and-response phrases

fields.label: Concept
fields.value: Question and Answer

fields.label: Exercise
fields.value: Play a "question" phrase (ending high), then "answer" it (ending low)

cards.title: Horn Sections
cards.description: Short, rhythmic phrases with clear attack and release

fields.label: Concept
fields.value: Punchy, Articulated Lines

fields.label: Exercise
fields.value: Study James Brown horn parts, recreate the rhythmic feel on guitar

cards.title: Classical Music
cards.description: Take a simple motif and develop it through variation and repetition

fields.label: Concept
fields.value: Motivic Development

fields.label: Exercise
fields.value: Play a 3-note motif, then vary it rhythmically, melodically, harmonically

cards.title: Attack Variation
cards.description: How hard you pick or fret notes

fields.label: Effect
fields.value: Changes tone color and perceived volume

cards.title: Note Duration
cards.description: How long notes are allowed to ring

fields.label: Effect
fields.value: Creates rhythmic interest and musical punctuation

cards.title: Spacing & Rests
cards.description: Strategic use of silence between notes

fields.label: Effect
fields.value: Creates tension, allows music to breathe, emphasizes important notes

fields.label: Effect
fields.value: Creates emotional peaks and valleys, builds tension

cards.title: David Gilmour - "Comfortably Numb"
cards.description: Creates emotional intensity and longing through minimal notes, maximum expression

fields.label: Technique
fields.value: Long sustained bends with slow, wide vibrato

cards.title: B.B. King - "The Thrill is Gone"
cards.description: Vocal-like phrasing that tells a story with every note

fields.label: Technique
fields.value: Short, punchy phrases with signature vibrato and note bending

cards.title: Gary Moore - "Still Got the Blues"
cards.description: Raw emotional power through extreme expression techniques

fields.label: Technique
fields.value: Aggressive vibrato, dramatic bends, dynamic volume swells

cards.title: John Mayer - "Gravity"
cards.description: Modern blues phrasing with sophisticated rhythmic placement

fields.label: Technique
fields.value: Laid-back timing, subtle bends, controlled vibrato

cards.title: Playing Behind the Beat
cards.description: Playing slightly after the beat creates a laid-back, bluesy feel. Common in blues, R&B, and some rock styles.

fields.label: Practice
fields.value: Use a metronome, deliberately play notes slightly after the click while maintaining the groove.

cards.title: Playing Ahead of the Beat
cards.description: Playing slightly before the beat creates urgency and drive. Common in rock, metal, and aggressive playing styles.

fields.label: Practice
fields.value: Play notes slightly before the metronome click, maintaining steady tempo while creating forward motion.

practiceSection.title: Phrasing Development Exercises
items: Mirror Exercise: Record yourself humming or singing a melody. Then try to exactly recreate the phrasing, including breathing spots, on guitar. Develops natural musical phrasing.
Single Note Exploration: Play just one note for 30 seconds. Use different attacks, vibrato speeds, bends, and dynamics to create interest. Develops expression without relying on note choice.
Call & Response: Play a short phrase (2-4 notes), then "answer" it with a different phrase. Practice musical conversation. Develops phrase structure and musical dialogue.
